utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Both parties have announced that they had preliminary matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic can go first.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic, you go first. And then Mr. Weber will think about what his preliminary matters --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- were. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just actually want Mr. Weber to put on the record the position of the OTP in regard of two documents. So the first one is P6889 MFI, and the second one is P6888. We want to know the position of the OTP, whether they claim it's -- those documents were created by Serb authorities, how they got these documents, and when.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, who drafted it is a question which seems to be not in the same area as where they come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean, if they are authentic, then whoever may have drafted them, and that may have some impact on how to interpret the documents and how to understand them and to -- but the first questions are: Where do they come from? Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And I appreciate what you just said. I'm just going to provide more detailed information than I already provided yesterday. At issue are two reports that are from the Trnovo DB. It is our position based on the language in the documents -- in both documents, the references in them, the names of the individuals, and how they -- especially the second document, 6889, how it parallels the minutes of who was present including police personnel, that they are in fact drafted by individuals of Serb ethnicity who were playing a part in these events. So that would be our basis of why we believe that -- yeah, well, they're from the Trnovo DB and why we believe that they were authored by individuals with direct knowledge of these events. In terms of the recovery of these documents, as I mentioned yesterday, it occurred during the reintegration process which included recovery of materials from various municipalities after the war surrounding Sarajevo. This -- this -- these two documents were items 573 and 574 recovered from the Trnovo municipality. I do not have specific information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please slow down --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: My information just indicates that the box came from police political authorities. I don't have very specific information as to a specific building. Aside from that, it was provided to the OTP by AID Sarajevo on the 18th of May, 2001. That's the information we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just wondering - I've looked at the documents as well - what it is specifically that the references and the names makes you believe that it's not, if I could express it this way, is not the result of successful spying activity rather -- but rather from an internal source. That's -- could you be a bit more precise? Because I have no difficulties in following you, that there seems to be a match with the minutes here and there. But even if I'm an intelligence officer, I would take care that there is a good match because that makes the information reliable. Therefore, could you explain a bit better what, perhaps not necessarily now immediately, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What I'm deriving this for is based on the individuals who were present at those meetings, which included police personnel, members of the security services, and the fact that they are also mentioned in the same context of those meetings present in here. Then there is also references, which would make them a logical source for the information, and then on top of it that there is references then to commanders and company commanders sending orders or information to the -- to the Crisis Staff or to other individuals in the documents. So based on the context of the discussion of how that's communicated, it would be our position that it is -- it is from a source with direct personal knowledge and involvement in the events --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- and we've seen who these people are based on those minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Mr. Lukic, any need for you at this moment to respond or?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do not want to respond. Although, our position is that this document is not created by Serb authorities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: They -- there might be some documents used in creating these documents, but we'll try to clarify this with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll then wait for that. Those were your preliminary issues. Mr. Weber, yours now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. It's with respect to P3207. This is the statement of Mr. Radulovic. The Prosecution wanted to inform the Chamber that an unredacted version is now available in e-court under 65 ter number 30594A. The second part of this is that -- is with respect to P6980, that document can be made a public exhibit. Change the status.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was -- yesterday we said that it should provisionally be under seal. Madam Registrar, the status of P6890 is now public. For the other one, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I also have to inform Your Honours that we attached -- that we asked for the B/C/S translation to be attached to one document -- actually, this information report we provided with this witness. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was still dealing at this moment with P3207 because two documents were -- the Prosecution wants P3207 to be admitted in an unredacted format.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that you gave us some time yesterday to respond to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you wish to do that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll -- the Chamber is aware that 30594a is now uploaded into e-court, but we'll wait for Mr. Lukic's submissions before we decide whether that can replace the redacted version which is in evidence now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Understood, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you raised a different matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which was?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In regard of D736, information report. The B/C/S translation is uploaded into the system under ID doc number 1D17-0307.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think we had reserved a number for that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's D736.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, D736. That number was reserved. We'll not decide immediately on admission. But, Madam Registrar, the B/C/S version may be attached to the original. I think it was not only a reserved number but it was even MFI'd. Is that correct, Madam Registrar, that it was MFI'd?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then leave is hereby granted and you're instructed to attach the B/C/S version to this -- to D736. The number just given by Mr. Lukic was 1D17-0307. Then I have one item which should be dealt with in private session and it will not take very long, but we have to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. And I think it would be time already for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom. I have one short item. During the testimony of Mane Djuric, the Defence tendered a document bearing 65 ter number 1D02733. The decision on admission of this 40-page document was deferred pending an agreement between the parties concerning ethnicity of the people listed in the document and about the number of pages which should be received in evidence. The Chamber would like to know whether the parties have come to an agreement, and if so, what that agreement is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution is checking right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could inform you at the outset of the next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Mr. Vlaski.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vlaski, you'll now be re-examined by Mr. Lukic. You know where to find him. And I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Vlaski.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are not going to take very long this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have Exhibit P6888 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise, is it D688 because this D6888 doesn't exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: P, sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So it's P6888.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vlaski, this morning we heard from the Prosecutor that this document was received from AID Sarajevo on the 18th of May, 2001, and we heard that it is the position of the Prosecution that this document had been created by the Serb side. The position of the Defence is that this document had been created by the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, this is totally inappropriate. I mean, in cross-examination there is a duty to inform the witness about your position if he contradicts that position. You are not supposed to tell the witness what you would like to hear and what you would like to have confirmed. That is in examination-in-chief totally inappropriate. I just leave it to that for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vlaski, it is written here that this is information on the operation activities of the Main Staff of the TO and command personnel of SR of the armed forces of Trnovo from the 15th of May to the 30th of May, 1992. As you can see from the document, it is not evident who this was sent to. According to the rules of your service --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I think that we're getting back again into a leading component in this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You're supposed not to tell the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- unless there is an agreement on it. And now I take it, Mr. Weber, that you would have easily agreed on that the addressees are not mentioned in the document. But you are supposed not to do that, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vlaski, can we see who this document was sent to? Can we see that from the document itself? Can one see from the document who it was sent to?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this document one cannot see who it was sent to, and the information contains data that the author of this information received in the period from the 15th of May to the 30th of May. That is precisely the period when the authors were not aware of the data because they did not know about the content of the conclusions of the organs of the TO of the Serb Republic, as it says here SR of Trnovo. That happened later on the basis of an analysis of the documentation that was accessible to them. Now which period that is, it is very hard to establish. It is only handwriting experts that could do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, a few questions. Have you seen the whole of the document, every single page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, these few things that are here were sufficient for me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If that's your level of drawing conclusions, that is -- I would like to -- you to be aware that it's impossible to say that a document does not show something if you've not seen the whole of the document. That's one. Second, you're saying that the authors were not aware. Who is the author of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The author of this document in all likelihood would be somebody from the security structures of the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, what is in all likelihood is not something we expect a witness to tell us. Apart, Mr. Lukic, that here of course you have the effect of your leading the witness. But you say in all likelihood you don't know, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I cannot make assertions but on the basis of what I see here, knowing the circumstances involved in that period of time, I can say that they did not have this information. They did not have complete information about the content that has been presented here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us what tells you that the author of this document did not have full information? And could you also explain to us how you can draw such a conclusion if you have not seen the whole of the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Information is provided here from 13 meetings, and from here we can see only three meetings on the first page. Having just partially seen the content of these meetings on the 15th, 16th, and 17th, that I took part in as well, it can be seen that this information was analysed subsequently on the basis of more complete information that they had gathered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you have seen the pages in between which refer to many more meetings? You are not aware of that? Witness, we are here to hear your knowledge about facts, not your assumptions or your conclusions and especially not, as it has been clearly shown over the last few minutes, that they do not have a proper basis in an accurate analysis of what you say is the basis of your conclusions. Mr. Lukic, I'm afraid that this is part of the whole problem with this witness's statement. Could you please not add to the problems but try to resolve them. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vlaski, in whose hands was Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Trnovo is a municipality where control changed three times: Once it was the Serb forces, the second time was the Bosniak Muslim forces, and then again the Serb forces. Parts of the municipality, not the entire municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At a certain moment, did the Muslim forces control the town itself?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us take a look at the last page. We see here that it says at the bottom: "SDB Department Trnovo." Do you see the signature?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just see this typewritten text: "SDB Department Trnovo." I see that typewritten. There is no signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see who the author of this text is?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The author is the department of the SDB. That is what is stated in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, ask the witness questions on specific knowledge he has but don't ask him to tell us what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This Chamber can read.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When I tried that you said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This Chamber --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- that I cannot ask him but I should ask him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- open questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But no useless questions. I mean, if you ask him whether you would -- we see in the signature area, which is not a signature but where the author is indicated, whether we see three words in B/C/S and four words in English. Of course the witness will say that he sees that, but the Chamber can see that as well. The Chamber can see as well that there is no signature. You don't have to ask a witness, unless he has specific knowledge about the document, why it was not signed or whether there is a signed version elsewhere, but don't ask him to tell us what is obvious from the document itself and which the Chamber can read as good or perhaps even better than the witness. We can see that. I can see that there is no signature. Don't ask the witness for that. Either he confirms that and then it's useless information, or he denies it and then we say it's unreliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you can, but I asked you not to add to the problems but to -- to make them less, not worse. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vlaski, is it customary to have such a document signed or not in the SDB?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is usual that the heading of the document should say, on the first page, what the institution is. Where this department of the SDB is. It should have said: "Ministry of the Interior, State Security Service." It should be someone that is the entity that this SDB department belongs to. That is what is lacking in this document. There is no protocol or register. There is no date when the document was created.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We heard that AID provided these documents to the Prosecution. Whose service is AID?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the service that was created after the security service of the Muslim side was transformed into the Agency for Investigations and Documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What does AID have to do with Pogorelica?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is one of the reasons why this transformation took place of the State Security Service into this Agency for Investigations and Documentation, because precisely at that time a Bosniak congress was held in Sarajevo where a decision was made -- or, rather, where an attempt was made to create a Muslim state in that part that was under the control of the authorities from Sarajevo. In relation to that, these security structures were transformed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, from the answer, I don't understand how Pogorelica is related to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Judge Moloto was asking what Pogorelica has to do with AID?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pogorelica is the result of co-operation of a few years between this intelligence organisation in Sarajevo with the Islamic intelligence service and instructors that were coming to the area that was engulfed by war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said Islamic. From which country?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Iran.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And was that -- did that have any links with terrorism?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time IFOR units felt that in that facility --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What's the relevance of this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: They said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- that they had received these documents from AID, Sarajevo AID. This is exactly the relevance. Because we have all the rights to suspect in anything provided by AID. And we'll especially show it in the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness may answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But also my problem here, Mr. Lukic, is that you suggested to the witness that there was terrorism involved instead of asking him the question and letting him give you the answer. Again, it is another leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We had that discussion with one of the Prosecution witnesses before, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, not with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are leading this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But he has Pogorelica in his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't know what Pogorelica is, but just don't lead the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the fact that we have received in evidence materials which would support your suggestions in your leading questions doesn't make the questions any less leading and do not make them any less inappropriate. Apparently you have not a good understanding of this type of procedural standards.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just draw Your Honours' attention to paragraph 19 of the -- this witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it is -- let me see. Mr. Lukic, if the matter is raised by the witness here, then I would agree with you it's not leading. But your response was not the witness talked about it himself but you said, "We had that discussion with one of the Prosecution witnesses before," which is an answer which at least confuses me. If you say we find the basis for this witness talking about this and not leading him in this respect in his own statement, that that's a totally different answer which might well be an acceptable answer. That's -- I have no problems with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll check that and you -- meanwhile, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you spoke about Pogorelica in your statement. While you were working in the State Security Service before the war, in the joint service, were documents altered by the Muslim part of the service?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war it would happen, including in this case where data was, so to say, treated relating to Young Muslims. There was information that during a search some foreign publications were left behind in order to be able to process this group, to charge them. So this was inappropriate, but somebody from the service felt that it was all right to do something like this in order to provide evidence. And then if we're talking about the wartime period, then there were no rules.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Lukic please repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to draw the Chamber's attention to paragraph 44 of the witness's statement where it says that no mention was made in official documentation about unlawful and anti-constitutional action by Muslims and Croats and their political police and paramilitary structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But now we can look at the following document received from AID.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is P6889.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The document is similar to the previous one. It says that this is a report on the activities and operation of the Trnovo SDS Municipal Board. Can you tell from the document to whom it was sent?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just like in the previous document, crucial elements are missing here in order to be able to identify the document. As this is about who the author is, representing which institution, and in the document you can see that it was drafted pursuant to a specific request because it discusses the activities and operation of the Trnovo SDS in the period from the 1st of January, 1992, to the 31st of May, 1992. In the previous case, the document referred to the Territorial Defence. This means that in the case of both documents they were requested, the information was requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will read the first paragraph. "The SDS Main Board and the Crisis Staff held 24 meetings in this period. The questions of preparing and organising the Serb people for armed rebellion against the Muslim people were mainly discussed at this meeting. This is supported by the following details ..." Thus, someone is asking for confirmation of the assertions made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe that last part is leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says in the text, if I -- I can ask the witness, but the Chamber instructed me not to ask him what's visible from the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is visible from the document that somebody asks for confirmation of something. That's the question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is end leading and -- Mr. Lukic, what we can read, we can read. Don't ask the witness about that. If you say the document states this and this and this and then you ask him a question about his personal knowledge about these matters, no problem. But don't ask the witness whether the document consists of four pages, because we can count to four.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I exactly tried that way with the first document, then you said I have to ask open questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm not spending any more time on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You apparently do not understand what I am telling you and that is a problem, but can't resolve it at this very moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, was your question not answered in the previous answer? He says there it was drafted pursuant to a specific request. So what you say that it's a report to somebody is actually the opposite of what the -- the corollary of what he's saying? You're asking a question that has already been answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll move on because we need a sentence in the seventh paragraph, and it's dealing with a -- we need next page in English version. It's dealing with the 7th of March of 1992. No, I -- still it's on the previous page of English version, sorry. The last -- probably the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In a sentence saying the matter of preparing the Serb people of Trnovo for "defence" was discussed at an SDS Municipal Board meeting on the 7th of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see what's written.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just -- just -- just one moment, please. While you were working or while you were attending the Crisis Staff sessions, did you notice that the Serb side is putting its own defence, the term "defence" in quotes, quotation marks?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, such a word or term was never placed in quotation marks in any documents. It was just used, and it was not accented like that in real life, either. At least that applied to that micro-locality in view of the ethnic composition of the local population.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And these quotes, do they indicate something else?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's evident that the author intended to interpret this defence, the term, in a different way, that it was an alleged defence and that it should have stood for some kind of aggressive or offensive action.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you this yesterday. I will read --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need the previous page in the English version, bottom of the page 2. We start from: "The 29th of May, 1992 ..." And the -- we have an issue with the translation of English version. It will be shown during my reading of this text.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "On the 29th of May, 1992, the Serbian Crisis Staff reached a decision for the entire Serbian population to move out in the direction of Sirokari and Dobro Polje with the explanation that they would be attacked by the Muslim forces, whereas in fact it was a matter of preparation for an armed intervention against Trnovo." Then the next date is the 31st of May, 1992. "In the morning at 0830 hours, the aggression on Trnovo and surrounding Muslim villages began." Who used the term "aggression" and "aggressor"?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, before I begin my answer to the question, it's clear who used the terms "aggression" and "aggressor." These were terms used by the Muslim side, even though Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina were the indigenous population, this includes Trnovo. There were no forces from the outside. These were neighbours. And what preceded the aggression was the attack on the village of Sirokari, when I was in that village, when the Muslim forces led by police and reserve force elements made an incursion into the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please answer the question rather than expound on matters not asked. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And I'm not finding the word "aggression." I see at 8.30 hours on --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly. We said we had an issue with the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we should --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's in B/C/S version --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We should first then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We see the term in the B/C/S version --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- in the penultimate line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "Agresija," fourth word from the semi-last line -- fourth word from the -- from the end. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vlaski, when you were still in the SDB during this period, would you say that the SDB of Republika Srpska or the National Security Service used the word "aggression" for a Serb attack anywhere?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was not possible. I myself drafted the first information that was sent to the National Security Service from this region regarding the attack by a paramilitary, a Green Berets unit, as it was passing through the settlement and when three policemen were killed. Actually, two of those Muslims were -- two of those policemen were Muslims. And when statements were taken, they were taken both from Muslim policemen and from other citizens who were eye-witnesses and were familiar with this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What I'm interested in right now is the word "aggression." Would the Serbian side designate its attack on the village of Trnovo as aggression in its own documents?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it would never do that. That term would not have been used ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. And reporting on Serb actions by Serb forces, did you ever use the term "aggression"?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an inappropriate term because in Bosnia and Herzegovina, all three people should have been living equally together. So at one point in time, the Croats were also proclaimed as aggressors even though they constitute 50 per cent of the population. So this word, "aggression," this term is completely out of place and I don't really -- wouldn't really want to dwell on it much more.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which side used that term?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most often it was the Muslim side and sometimes in some areas in the beginning the Croat side, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now regarding paragraph 44 of your statement. I already quoted it briefly today, and you said as a result of the organisational and personnel structure in place wherein Serbian personnel did not have any influence, there were cases of falsified information. No mention was made in official documents about unlawful and anti-constitutional actions by Muslims and Croats and their political police and paramilitary structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So let us now look at document P6634.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document was shown to you yesterday by the SDB of Sarajevo from the 31st of March, 1992, minister of internal affairs of BH, subject forwarding an information. And the document states: "We are hereby forwarding you the list of employees of the SRBH MUP who took part in the activities related to setting of barricades in the region of Sarajevo in early March 1992 ..." Yesterday we saw that you were shown that Mandic Momcilo, Dragisa Kujacic, Velimir Przulj, took part in this. Do you know if it was properly reported who killed the Serb best man from the wedding party? Who erected the barricades?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I answer? You can see from this document that it was written on the 13th of March, 1992, whereas the events that it refers to happened in the period of March 1st. So in the period of 13 days. This is a very dilettante sort of information. It's not properly worked through and does not deal with all the problems that cropped up in that period. It's one-sided. It doesn't provide any context in which the incidents occurred. It does not explain the causes or the effect of the events. It just noted the names of certain persons who were meant to be disqualified in a professional and political sense in a way. I myself was an eye-witness of all of these events and I am very much aware of everything that was happening in that period, because during that period and far earlier than that, Muslim paramilitary formations blockaded certain roads in the old city area in the neighbourhood of facilities being used by the JNA. And together with police representatives, they stopped and blocked convoys that were passing through with the authorisation of the Ministry of Internal Affairs; in particular, the illegal activities of paramilitary units after the event in the Kosevo hospital when they blocked a health centre, and then these paramilitary formations ID'd all those who would come to the hospital centre. They were armed, these formations that were doing these identity checks. So this information does not give any -- any information about those aspects of these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just briefly, these paramilitary Muslim formations, did they stop any members of your family at the entrance into the hospital?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did. And I was stopped when I came to have my wound bandaged at the time when I came to the hospital. I left in an ambulance because I wasn't sure how things would go. We used an ambulance to leave Sarajevo because I wasn't sure what kind of consequences could follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P6886, briefly. Could we take a look at that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm interrupting you. How much more time would you need? You said yesterday you would need half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not much means how much?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll try to finish in five, six minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll do that after the break and I'll -- but before we take the break, I'm seeking clarification on one issue, Mr. Lukic, which is behind us already. I can do that after the break as well. Perhaps that's better. If the witness would follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break and will resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll wait for the witness to enter the courtroom. Meanwhile, Mr. Lukic, I can inform you that the distribution list for the decision of the 2nd of October includes you and Mr. Stojanovic as being the addressees of to whom they were sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is possible. Our computers are not still working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were they not working on the 2nd of October -- oh, you say you cannot verify.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, I cannot verify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You cannot verify at this moment. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I believe so but I cannot verify yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The title is: "Reasons for denial of ..." and then the name of the motion, submitted by Trial Chamber I on the 2nd of October, 2014. Mr. Lukic, you -- although you used even in net time more than the 30 minutes you announced yesterday, you have another five to six minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We need pages 3 in B/C/S and 4 in English of this document that is on our screens, which is P6886.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vlaski, we have to move quickly. Please, just take a look at the first line of this document. Number 1 says: "Nedjo Vlaski, paid in SNB." What does that mean, paid in SNB?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received a decision in the SNB, the security service, the National Security Service, and I don't know who put me on this list. I was wounded and I was being treated in Trnovo, and I guess that these colleagues thought that they should put me on their list so that my interests would be met, although I had actually been in the SNB. That is where my job was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Column 5 where it says "signature," is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not sign this document. I've never seen this document. This is the first time I am seeing this document. Actually, yesterday and today.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you just see what is written?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "ispl." That would be short for "isplacen," paid out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then that is crossed out, right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's crossed out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now briefly the next document, P6887. This is a record of the meeting of the Crisis Staff in Trnovo held on the 29th of April. We need page 6 in English and 8 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This was discussed yesterday. On this page --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, the transcript page was 27811. That's the reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So what was discussed was this attack; namely, Edo attacking Hamo Karic. Edo is Edhem Godinjak, that's what you said.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, chief of the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the ethnicity of Edhem Godinjak and Hamo Karic?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're ethnic Muslims or, rather, Bosniaks as it is called now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did one of them work for the Serb side or were they both on the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were engaged on the Muslim side. They had some internal problems of their own.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Down here it says: "Nedjo: All problems can be overcome." Are these your words?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll just go briefly to P68980 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Lukic. You are recorded to have said 68980. That's 69.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. P6980.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] That's a document that was signed "Milos." Let us look at the last page now, briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You see the signature down here, "Milos." You've already commented upon this document, but now I would like to ask you the following. Now that you have seen the first and second page, since this is an Official Note, is the form of this Official Note right?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just like in the case of AID, we also unfortunately had these para-intelligence structures in our own ranks and they acted outside the chain and the rules of service. Therefore, these documents are not satisfactory from a formal point of view and also in terms of essence. Professionally they are not proper. I have examples of such notes here with me, what notes should look like, with all the elements that are necessary. If anybody is interested, I can hand them over so that you can compare. However, I spoke here for reasons of substance -- I do apologise. This is also information that was ordered because this structure acted in the interest of some other intelligence and security service.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you another thing briefly: Was the addressee supposed to be referred to here?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, certainly. There would have to be some designation, first of all, the immediate superior of this structure or group that acted outside the system for it to be part of regular co-operation with an agency. However, all of this was extra-institutional and therefore these constructs are possible. For what purpose and on the basis of what kind of needs, that would require a broader explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This group, when was it most active?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was active from the beginning, in 1991, all the way up until 1994, when we decided to cut off not only the activity of this organisation but also others like Typhoon. I personally took part in the charges that were brought against that group and also the author of this Official Note.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You personally talked to the author?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only him but also a few other members from this para-intelligence group.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just my last question, sir. What was mentioned was that you testified in the Stanisic/Zupljanin case. Who called you to testify in that case?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Office of the Prosecutor, in order to establish the truth about all the things that were happening in this period that I am testifying about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vlaski. We certainly won't have any more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vlaski.

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you realise that in your statement you rely on multiple documents provided by AID?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear the question from the very beginning because I got the interpretation late, so could you please repeat what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd be happy to. Do you realise that in your statement you rely on multiple documents provided by AID?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Provided by AID? We did not have any insight into documents provided by AID. We had insight into documents that we obtained through our own operative work.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I imagine that you're not aware of this. But as associated exhibits that you comment on in your statement - specifically, paragraphs 62 and 48 - do you realise that those documents were provided AID?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is, I think, pretty broad. It should be shown to the witness. How can he know?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if the witness has commented on a document, you can ask a question. Of course, if he doesn't remember, it should be shown to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, Mr. Lukic, the Prosecution may expect that the witness is aware of the documents he commented on, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And actually it's our position that the witness is probably not aware of this since this is information that would be known to the OTP as to where the documents were provided from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Now the witness is supposed to know the documents but you now add another aspect - that is, that they are coming from the AID.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. First of all, if you look at paragraph 62 -- it's both documents, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's specifically P2984.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the decision of the BiH Presidency and what it shows. Were you aware that its provenance is the AID?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, these are documents that were published in the Official Gazette. This is not an AID document. These documents were published in the Official Gazette and everybody who works in the state organs was duty-bound to be informed about these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's not my question, sir. I get that AID provides documents that were authored by others, similar to the ones that you've seen earlier today. My question is: Were you aware that those documents had been provided to the Office of the Prosecutor by AID?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, Mr. Weber, the witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How can I know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness -- that's -- one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's exactly -- he's answered it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it -- the witness says that this document is a document published in the Official Gazette. Is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And the other one is not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. But we -- let's first deal with the first one. Is it of any use to find out and would you be surprised if the witness would look at the document which is in the Official Gazette and considers it irrelevant, whether you copied the Official Gazette that was delivered to the AID or to the UN or to the government of Spain or -- I mean, Official Gazette is Official Gazette. So therefore, whether it was received from the AID, at least at this moment the relevance of that question escapes me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It actually doesn't go to as much as the Official Gazette or not. I'm just trying to establish that the witness has a lack of knowledge that documents -- multiple documents that he comments on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- we just went to the first one here and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Choose one which is more convincing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I think the witness has said that he was not aware of the -- and that's all I was trying to establish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I commented on it --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that it's totally irrelevant whether you receive -- whether you have bought the Official Gazette at the bookshop at the corner, whether you received it from the AID, whether you -- Official Gazette is Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I think we're getting sidetracked. The witness says he's not aware so I'm going to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So yesterday, sir, when you were shown Exhibit P6888 at transcript page 27815, you stated: "The events that were referred to from the SDS Department of Trnovo are something that I'm seeing for the first time because I had left the area already on the 13th of May and I did not come back ever to this municipality, so that I do not know what happened after the 13th of May."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you repeat that P number?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm referring to a transcript page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- 271815, when the witness was -- during the witness being shown P6888.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Triple 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'll read the last sentence here of what you said: "So whatever the events were there after the 13th of May, I am not aware of what happened." Today when you were shown Exhibit P6888 at transcript page 12, you stated: "Information is provided here from 13 meetings, and from here we can see only three meetings on the first page. Having just partially seen the content of these meetings on the 15th, 16th, and 17th, that I took part in as well, it can be seen that this information was analysed subsequently on the basis of more complete information that they had gathered." Based on the inconsistent answers you have provided to this Chamber, one claiming that you did not know what happened after the 13th of May and the other claiming you actually took part in meetings between the 15th and 30th of May, is it correct that you have not told the truth to this Chamber?

utterances.speaker: NEDJO VLASKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said the truth. As for what is mentioned in this information, from the aspect of how it was written up formally and from the point of view of substance, until the 13th of May I was following certain events. After that, not. And they are referred to in this information which is compound information. For all these things that happened between the 1st and the 31st.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you told us today that you attended the meetings. The meetings 15th, 16th, and 17th of May. At the same time you told us that you had left on the 13th of May. That is the matter on which I'd like you to focus your answer to start with.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I misspoke, that it was the 15th, 16th, and 17th, because at the time I really wasn't there. Probably I wasn't focused enough on my answer when I gave it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You referred to the reference 15th, 16th of May, which you saw on the first page of that document. You said -- you referred to all of the meetings and you said, "the ones I see on the first page," which were after the 13th of May, that you attended them. Any explanation for -- that's not misspeaking, that is referring to a specific date mentioned in the document and you said: "What is said about that meeting is not accurate because they were misinformed. I attended those meetings." That's the basis for your knowledge why you told us that the report was inaccurate. Any explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not have enough information about the dates. All I know is that the first meetings that I attended were actually in April, not in May. But I did not pay attention to that detail, that it was after the 13th. Because on the 13th, I left the area and I think that I was in Belgrade then. I couldn't comment on this, really. But the first three meetings during April, in that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness -- Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- period I was in that area, so in that context I was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are commenting on a document and you say what is said here, and that is only mid-May, that document didn't say anything about the April meetings on the page you refer to, "I know that it's inaccurate, they were not well informed," and you give us the basis for your judgement because it's opinion and judgement anyhow, your presence during those meetings. And this turns out not to be true. What are we supposed to do with this kind of evidence, Witness? That's a question you don't have to answer, but ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My reaction was rushed, I said that. I didn't pay attention to the dates. So I spoke in the context of the contents of the documents, and then I remembered that I was in a few previous meetings of the Crisis Staffs and that the analysis included all the meetings. But as for the period of the 13th, I myself was not in that area. So I wasn't focused enough on the dates. I know that there were -- the first meetings that I participated in were in April but the information refers to May, and as of the 13th I was no longer there. I'm sorry, it was my error in answering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, today I put it to you that based on the record that we have today before you made that comment, that it was made quite clear to you that it related to meetings and events between the 15th and 30th of May and that you are now just giving excuses when, in fact, you intentionally lied to this Chamber. Do you have any other comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection. I don't think that we use this word in this courtroom. We were able to use it many times during our cross-examinations of their witnesses. We never used it. And I think in this Tribunal this word is not permitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, although the Chamber would have preferred --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Mr. Weber, that you would have said that the witness was intentionally not telling the truth, but that comes down to the same. Do you have any comment on what Mr. Weber said, that you intentionally were not telling us the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not saying this intentionally. I was not focused on the dates that I was looking at. I was focused on the content of the information that we were looking at. I wasn't concentrating on the dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the content was about what was discussed during those meetings, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These topics were discussed at all the meetings at the time that I was there as well. It's not just these meetings that are referred to in the records. There were daily meetings and contacts with those people during this critical period, so I don't know who wrote which records when because I didn't see any of those minutes or records of the meetings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has heard your explanation. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it was your witness so this was the last round. No further questions from you. No further questions from the Bench, no further questions from the Prosecution, which means that this concludes your evidence, your testimony in this court, Mr. Vlaski. I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and I would also like to thank you for having answered all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and you may now follow the usher. And I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the Prosecution -- is the Defence ready to call its next witness, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we are, Your Honour. Only I think that we might maybe discuss associated exhibits now or if you want us to postpone it for tomorrow, whatever you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber is ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We reduced a number of the documents so -- as Judge Moloto instructed us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And let me see. The position of the Prosecution on the associated exhibits would be the following, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This could take some time. So the first one I think that we had left off at was 1D03114. There was an objection based on the relevance of the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- and lack of a date context which I think the Defence indicated that they did not know. The witness does comment on the document and this was one of the documents from AID. So based on re-examination, I'm going to actually withdraw my objection and ask to have it admitted based on the way the witness commented on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The next one is 1D03115. The Prosecution has no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Then let's take them one by one. We go back to the previous one. Madam Registrar, 1D03114 would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document receives number D743, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D743 is admitted. 1D03115 would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D744, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. We move to the next one, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We object based on the grounds of reliability and relevance. We do not know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the next one is?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. 1D03121.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We object based on the grounds of reliability and relevance. These appear to be handwritten notes. It's not clear to us who they're from or what the temporal context of these notes are. We did request origin information, which I'm not aware of right now. And also the Prosecution inquired of the Defence whether these were the complete notes. So those were the matters related to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll withdraw this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Withdrawn. Next one is 1D05124. A translation was pending.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. We have had the opportunity to review the translation. We indicated to the Defence that we would have no objection provided the Defence gave us the origin information and established some personal knowledge foundation with the witness which they have not. So based on the fact that they have not done that, we object to the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe we should MFI this one, and if we find a way to provide more information, then we would ask for admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection against it being MFI'd?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1D05124, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number D745, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D745 is marked for identification. Next one is 1D05127.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Similar to the handwritten notes we just discussed, the Prosecution objects based on reliability and relevance. There is also no temporal indication to these handwritten notes or a context in the notes, and it's unclear who they're from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: They are from this witness, but I -- that's true, I didn't ask him. So we withdraw this one because there is no other way to establish it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution objects based on reliability and relevance. This is purportedly an intercepted conversation involving Sefer Halilovic. There is no date to this conversation. The Prosecution did ask for a copy of the recording which the Defence did give to the Prosecution on the first day of this witness's testimony. We would note that both according to the transcripts that have been provided and also according to the recording, that the conversation appears incomplete. And the notes indicate the rest of the conversation was not reproduced because the tape broke. I also had the opportunity to look at the -- the property details, the electronic property details for the audio file that was provided to us, and they indicate that the file was modified on 1 January 1995. We have some concerns about the reliability of this material. We did ask the Defence to establish some context to this with the witness and the witness's knowledge about this recording and they have not, so we would oppose the -- its admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would propose then for this to be MFI'd. It would be easy probably with somebody else to establish that it was the voice of Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the concern seems not to be primarily whether it's the voice of Mr. Halilovic. The concern seems to be that the material has been tampered with, and that of course is a far more serious issue than the one you now refer to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tampered in which way? The tape [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The change --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The tape did break but it was put together later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It did break but it was put together --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just try to understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's what this witness told me, that he couldn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you haven't asked him anything about it, but let us just assume that that happens. If a tape breaks, that will stop the recording, yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During the reviewing the tape, not during the taping.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, typically questions you -- first of all, we do not know to what extent this witness knew about those details. And that is a general concern the Chamber has about the source of knowledge. But -- that certainly is an issue which -- but we would need more details from Mr. Weber what he or, may I take it, your experts or those who are knowledgeable about the matter told you and whether that is consistent with the explanation given by Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's not a matter of consulting with experts. I've given -- I've related all the information known to me and that's all we know at this time. You know, if the witness was the proper person to ask about this, they should have been asked about this, and we don't know where this tape is even coming from. It's been provided to us from the Defence. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we do understand that the Prosecution has asked for further details. You are now telling us in court what happened and you have not verified that with the witness. You have not given those details prior to today, from what I understand. Therefore, the Chamber is not willing at this moment to MFI this document. If you want to revisit the matter at a later stage, then we'll -- we'll then hear what the reasons are for the way in which you dealt with the matter until now and what are the reasons why you want to revisit the matter. But we -- at this moment, we'll not MFI the document under the present circumstances. The next one, Mr. Weber, would be 1D05133 if I'm well informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You are, Your Honour. And if I could try to expedite things a little bit more and also address the three after that: 1D05136 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just to make things shorter. The rest -- the rest of the documents, the three following documents we are not going to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the ones with last three digits 133, 136, and 139?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, sorry. 136, 139, 143 we are not going to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. 133 therefore stands, and there is no objection, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There is going to be, but obviously if they are withdrawing there is no need to make it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but for 1D05133 there is no objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No, there is an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is an objection, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Again, we objected -- we wanted to know the origin information of the document, and we asked the Defence, since it was unclear that the witness actually had personal knowledge of the document, to establish a foundation with the witness which they have not done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The truth is that I tried to deal with other things and I didn't have time. We didn't establish this so we -- maybe -- this document -- it's a written document, we would be using that one in the future for sure, so we can MFI that one. Actually, we ask Your Honours to MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the future, you mean with other witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: With other witnesses, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then since no questions were put to the witness, we'll wait until you would use that and we'll not MFI the document for the time being. But we're looking forward to you introducing the same document through another witness. 136, 139, 143 are not tendered anymore. Mr. Weber, may I take it that the Prosecution feels no need to --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If they are withdrawn, we have nothing further to state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And if they get used in the future, the Defence is aware of our considerations with respect to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we have 1D05250, the information from the proofing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I actually think that would be the clearest record for both the statement and the proofing -- the information report, to actually submit those in writing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Submissions are expected to be made in writing then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And having MFI'd this one already, I'm just wondering --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it has been MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, D736 MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D736. Then the last one is 26215, but I think we have decided on that one already and it was admitted, Official Note signed by Milos. Having dealt with this, any further matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. If I may be excused, if that's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are excused, Mr. Weber. Ms. Bibles, will it be you or will it be Mr. Jeremy who --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: It will be Mr. Jeremy, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then is the Defence ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe we are, Your Honours, and I believe the next witness is Mr. Ranko Kolar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could he be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You'd previously asked about 1D02733, whether the parties had reached agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: The parties have apparently not had an opportunity to discuss that yet. We would expect some discussion before Monday, probably a discussion after court tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'd like to hear Monday not later than midday.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kolar, I assume.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Mr. Kolar. I noticed already that even when giving your solemn declaration you have a speed of speech which will cause our interpreters certainly quite some problems. Could you try to speak slowly, otherwise perhaps part of your testimony would be lost and that's not what we are -- what we want to happen. You'll first be examined by Mr. Ivetic. You'll find him to your left. Mr. Ivetic is a member of the Defence team for Mr. Mladic. Mr. Ivetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And perhaps to assist the usher, I do have a clean copy of the witness's statement that I can give to the usher so as to save time later.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in the interim, Mr. Kolar, good day to you, sir. I would ask that you please state your full name for purposes of the record.

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Good day. Ranko Kolar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And at this time I would ask that the document 1D01708 be called up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, what we see on the screen now is a witness statement. Can you tell us if you recognise the signature on page 1?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Yes, that is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the last page in Serbian and page 4 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, there is a signature on this page as well. Can you tell us whose signature appears here?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: It's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, upon signing this statement, did you have a chance to read it in the Serbian language so as to ascertain if everything is accurately recorded therein?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is everything accurately recorded herein?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question? I didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Upon your review, did you determine that everything in your statement is accurately recorded?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, if I were to ask you today questions based on the same topics as contained in your written statement, would your answers be in essence the same as in your statement?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And since you have taken the solemn declaration today, does that mean that the answers as recorded in your statement are truthful?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would move for 1D01708 to be entered into evidence as the next Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. No objection to the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1708 receives number D746, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D746 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, there are no associated exhibits. I would thus now be prepared to read a short summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Witness Ranko Kolar lived in Prijedor when the war broke out but was assigned to the reserve forces of the 6th Sana Brigade of the JNA. Upon being mobilised, he was given the position of platoon commander within the 1st Company of the 1st Infantry Battalion with the rank of reserve lieutenant.
