During that time there were few Muslims and Croats in the unit as they had not wanted to respond to the mobilisation called. Also the few officers of non-Serb ethnicity in the command began to dissipate from the command. His unit was dispatched to parts of Croatia to defend locations, and 1st April 1992 was returned to Sanski Most per the agreement on the JNA's withdrawal from Croatia. The witness went on leave to Prijedor and his stay was extended when fighting erupted in Hambarine. His unit was engaged in unblocking friendly forces that were encircled by Croat Muslim forces in the Korenjovo village. The witness recalls that 150 personnel under the command of Amir Avdic surrendered to the Serbs and were transported with their weapons to the zone of the 5th Corps and in exchange the Avdic forces released 15 Serb soldiers. Towards the end of the war, the witness became brigade chief of staff and held the rank of major. That completes the summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Do you have any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I wish to look together at paragraph 4, which is to be found in page 2 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, you have a hard copy also in front of you. Here in paragraph 4 you use the term "ethnic intolerance." What do you mean when you use this term? What you are describing?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Well, specifically in 1991, I personally noticed that there was a lack of national tolerance among the peoples of Yugoslavia. The first example of that were open attacks against the members of the JNA already on the 6th of May, 1991, in Split, when an attempt was made to strangle, brutally, a military conscript who was of Macedonian ethnicity and another soldier fell victim in the barracks. There was another thing that I thought of. The first armed conflicts in Slovenia were launched by parts of the Slovenian Territorial Defence when members of the JNA were brutally attacked at border crossings and in Slovenia itself. Then in 1991, in June, our brigade had already been mobilised and most of the Croat and Muslim people, although they had responded to the first call up, they said that they didn't want to join the members of the JNA to restore law and order at the borders in Slovenia. All of this is a series of evidence and it would take a lot of time if I were to refer to each and every example. So all of this led to a lack of tolerance among the peoples of the Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just get clarification Mr. Lukic. Am I right, sir, to say that at that time the JNA was a multi-ethnic army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would you then say that an attack on the JNA is an ethnic issue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, you are supposed to speak at a level of volume not audible for others. Could you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please put the question to me once again? I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If the JNA was a multi-ethnic army, would you say an attack on the JNA - you've referred to attacks twice, one in Slovenia and another one on the JNA - would you regard an attack on the JNA as an ethnic issue, a reason for ethnic tensions? You are attacking the army which is multi-ethnic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that was one of the reasons of the inter-ethnic tensions and lack of tolerance amongst the peoples of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe -- I think we are talking at cross-purposes. What I am saying, if the Slovenian Territorial Defence attacks the JNA, how do you say that is an ethnic attack when the JNA is a multi-ethnic army? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think that the JNA at that time consisted of representatives of all the ethnic groups of the former Yugoslavia and it was one of the bases of the former Yugoslavia. The attack of the Slovenian Territorial Defence was an attack against the state of Yugoslavia itself. That is my opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's not ethnic. That's an attack on the state and the state has no ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, since the former Yugoslavia was a multi-ethnic state, that was one of the causes that led to the clashes among the peoples of the former Yugoslavia. One of the reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. I think I have asked my question. I leave it at that. Thank you so much, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I -- it is always my duty to correct somebody. Now I have to correct my colleague. It's Mr. Ivetic and not Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did I say that again?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's all right, Your Honours. I think we are at the time for the break, though. I'm not positive but I think it's there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I establish that there is no dispute about the matter raised a second ago. Witness, a mistake was made in addressing Mr. Ivetic. That explains this exchange of views. We'll take a break of 20 minutes and we would like to see you back after the break - that is, at quarter past 12.00. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not the Chamber but it's me personally who has to apologise for the late start.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But at least we should correct the transcript. We didn't resume at 12.32 but 12.23. That means it's a kind of excuse for our Presiding Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you would need the full 30 minutes of your estimate?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I may even come in under, but it won't be over, hopefully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd next like to look at paragraph 12 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Which we find on page 3 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Here, sir, you talk about going back to Prijedor and you mention fighting in Hambarine. Did you have occasion to become aware of what had triggered this fighting in Hambarine?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Yes, I did find out. That day I went for a holiday, a two-day holiday from Sanski Most to Prijedor. And then as soon as I arrived in Prijedor, after noon, you could hear shooting in the region of the Hambarine village and other villages in the area. That day I found out that the road where the Muslim forces were under the command of a certain Aliskovic, the evening before or a couple of evenings before was fired at at members of the JNA who had been in the Western Slavonia front who were returning home to Ljubija. That was when a request was made, if I can put it that way, by the forces of the Yugoslav People's Army that that section of the population or the -- of the population should hand in their weapons by a certain date.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since the weapons were not handed over, there was fighting which broke out in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, the interpreter did not catch the date that you said that the weapons should be handed in. I don't know whether you actually mentioned the date, but if you did, could you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, that was the 24th of May. I don't know if it was a Saturday. 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now I'd like to look together at paragraph 15 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Which is to be found on page 4 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, here you identify that 150 personnel headed by Amir Avdic surrendered to your forces and were delivered with their weapons back to the Muslim side. First, can you tell us if these are the same fighters that are referenced in the previous paragraph 13 in relation to the attempts to unblock, via Hrustovo village, the forces in Korenjovo village?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Yes, these are the Muslim formations headed by Amir Avdic, which, after fighting around Hrustovo and Vrhpolje, began negotiating with our forces. In the fighting they had captured 15 of our members and had withdrawn towards the Golaja woods. After the negotiations began with our forces, they were allowed to pass unhindered through our territory which was under the control of the then-Army of Republika Srpska of Bosnia and Herzegovina and our military police and with the help of the Red Cross. The agreement was that our 15 captured members of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina should also go with them up to Grabez. The exchange was carried out, according to what I heard. I wasn't there. I just heard about it. It was done with the help of the Red Cross in the line of separation with the 5th Corps of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Grabez, near the barracks, where about 150 members of the Bosnia and Herzegovina Army crossed over to the side of the 5th Corps, and these 15 captured soldiers of ours were returned to Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is kindly asked to speak more slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I would caution you to try to speak more slowly so that the interpreters can keep up with your speech. I know it's difficult. I have the same problem. I now would like to look at paragraph 16 of your statement where you state that your company was sent to other theatres of war. Can you please tell us about any other such theatres of war that you personally accompanied your unit to which stand out in your memory?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: During 1992 already, in late 1992, I assumed the duty of battalion commander. It was the infantry battalion of 500-strength. We went to a number of fronts with the battalion, I'm just going to mention one of them, and that is the theater when we went to intervene and help our forces in the Drina Corps sector on the 6th of January, 1993. We were helping to stop a Muslim operation carried out by Naser Oric from the 28th Muslim Division whose task was to cut off the road from Zvornik to Bratunac and to capture both of these towns. Then it's well known later what happened on the 7th of January, 1993, when practically 12 Serb villages, initially Kravica and then the other villages, were torched. We came there to intervene. We stopped Naser Oric and his units at the Banjevici-Ocenovici line, where we managed to stop his units and we managed to save a number of the civilian population that happened to be in that area. We managed to evacuate a number of those citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: First of all, these villages that were torched, who were they torched by?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: I personally watched from an observation post from where the village of Kravica and those other villages that I cannot remember can be seen very well. This was an OP at the village of Ocenovici. This was done by the Muslim forces who were moving in two echelons. The first echelon was moving and carrying out combat actions. The second echelon was moving and using horses and saddles. They were looting and robbing these Serbian houses, and then after that they burned the houses. The second echelon looked to be quite disorganised. They were moving in groups and practically everything that could be carried out of the appliances and food - primarily food - was taken out of those houses which were then subsequently burned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for my last topic, I'd like to ask you a few general questions. What kind of orders were given by your brigade command during the war in relation to the treatment of prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Each order regardless of whether it related to defensive or assault actions, the decision would also refer to the treatment of prisoners where it was decisively stated that captured soldiers or civilians, we must not mistreat them and we had to hand them over to the nearest command organ for intelligence and security affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what kind of orders were given as to engaging the enemy in or near populated areas?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: It was also clearly worded in the order, since I was a commander of the brigade -- no, I'm sorry, of the battalion. I apologise. I had orders from the brigade command with the signature of the brigade commander where it stated expressly: In inhabited places, open fire only at facilities from which resistance is coming with minimal destruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what steps were taken to communicate these orders both in relation to prisoners of war and opening fire in populated areas so that every soldier would know and understand them?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: The orders were conveyed along the hierarchy of the military line, from the written order of the brigade commander to battalion commander --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I will repeat it. The brigade commander would convey a written order to the battalion commanders. The battalion commanders would convey written orders to the komandirs of the companies. The commanders of the company would convey oral orders to platoon commanders, and then platoon commanders would convey the orders to each individual fighter or soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kolar, I thank you for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is the end of my direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Mr. Jeremy, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I am, thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kolar, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Jeremy. You find him to your right. And Mr. Jeremy is counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And good afternoon, Mr. Kolar.

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now to begin with, I'd like to get a brief overview of your military career history to the extent that it's not already covered in your statement or during direct examination today. So in your statement we read that you were commander of the 1st Infantry Company of the 1st Battalion. Now, when were you first appointed?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: I have first said that in September when I was mobilised I became a platoon commander and that was until January 1992. And then in January 1992, I was appointed as the commander of the 1st Infantry Company of the 1st Infantry Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now how many men were in your 1st Company?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: By establishment, the infantry company numbers from 110 to 120 men, and we usually did have that number of men in the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now your commander, the commander of the 1st Battalion, at this time in January through to July was Ranko Brajic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. Ranko Brajic was appointed only in June 1992 as battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So is it correct that in June and July 1992 Ranko Brajic was your battalion commander?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: In June, yes. But in July, in the first half of July, Ranko Brajic was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you. And at the time that he was killed, do you recall when where you were? Were you still in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: He was killed in the Bihac-Grabez plateau, he was killed in the direction of Bihac. And I was there at that time, along that axis with my unit. He was the battalion commander and I was the commander of the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And do you recall when your unit first went to this Bihac-Grabez plateau?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Yes, we were there for two days: On the 13th of June until the 14th of June. That's when I think we returned, in the evening. That was the first time. But it was just one company, the infantry company. Not the entire battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So just to confirm, at the time that Ranko Brajic was killed in July, you were not with him but instead you were in Sanski Most? Because I understand from your previous answer that you were -- you were in this Grabez area on the 13th and 14th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Yes. On the 13th and the 14th of June, I was there but it was only just one infantry company. I was a part of that company. I think this was on the 10th or the 11th of July. I don't remember precisely when Ranko Brajic was killed. The complete battalion was there and I was -- my company was there. I was the commander. So I was there when Ranko Brajic was killed. I wasn't really close to that place but I was in that sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Okay. But prior to the 10th of July, you were in Sanski Most; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Yes. Before the battalion left to the Grabez plateau, we were in Sanski Most for a period of time.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked not to come so close to the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Kolar, our interpreters are asking you not to come so close to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now the 1st Infantry Battalion was part of the 6th Brigade, the 6th Krajina Brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And the commander of the 6th Krajina Brigade during this January to July period was Colonel Branko Basara; correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now today you said that in late 1992 you became the commander of a 500-strength infantry battalion. This was the 2nd Infantry Battalion of the 6th Brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: No, it was the 5th Battalion of the 6th Sana Brigade. I was appointed to the post in late November 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Okay. Now in your statement you say that you -- later in the war, in 1995, you became chief of staff of the 6th Brigade. When were you appointed?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: I was appointed chief of staff of the brigade --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to repeat the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Witness, could you please repeat the dates that you were appointed chief of staff of the 6th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact date, but I think it was in late January 1995. That was the beginning. Because I handed the battalion over in late January, in Glamoc, and I was immediately appointed the chief of staff, so this was then in late January 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And how long did you hold this post of chief of staff until?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Until February 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you. And I would like to focus on Sanski Most in April 1992, and I've got a few questions about your locations and duties from this period onwards. And for orientation purposes, I'm going to call up a map of Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please see 65 ter 31557. And could we focus in on the top-third of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kolar, in paragraph 11 of your statement we read that you were a company commander and your main task was securing the main bridge in the town of Sanski Most. When did you first starting securing this bridge? What was the date?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: I cannot remember the date but it was sometime in mid-April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And do you see the bridge on the map in front of us?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, with the assistance of the usher, I'm going to ask you just to mark that bridge that you were guarding in mid-April 1992. Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we need that? There is only one bridge which seems not to be a railway bridge, Mr. -- or do you see more bridges?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I don't see more bridges.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, then -- well, the witness has marked it now not surprisingly at the one and only place where there is a bridge not being a railway bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. That's clear. Now, who gave you this task to guard the bridge?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: The battalion command or, rather, the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now in your statement and today, you've talked about your visit to Prijedor in May 1992. When did you return back from Prijedor? What was the date?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: I remember well that I returned on the 30th of May, 1992, because that was the day that the town of Prijedor was attacked from a number of directions by Muslim Croat forces. I returned in the late evening because I could not come in by the main road, the Prijedor-Sanski Most road. We had to go by the right bank of the river, then go to Prijedor, Usorci, Ostra Luka, that's where we crossed the bridge. And then in the afternoon I met up with my unit, the 1st Infantry Unit, in the sector of the village of Krkojevci.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, this village of Krkojevci that you've just mentioned, do you see it on the map that we have before us?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And could we go down a little bit on the map, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Then you will lose the marking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I think we can leave the marking because the bridge is obvious to us all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, the bridge is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I see Krkojevci.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to avoid any confusion, the bridge is just in -- crossing the river at the centre of what is indicated as being Sanski Most village.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And could we just move the map down a little bit please. That's great. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So, Witness, on the map before us, just to the right of the centre, I see the place name Krkojevci running north to south written in -- in a vertical way. That's the area that you -- that your unit was based; correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now was your unit providing security in this location?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: When I arrived, the unit was in the area of deployment. That is to say, that it did not provide security at that location. Rather, it was in the area of deployment and it was a reserve position.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Was your command post in -- based in Krkojevci, was that the purpose of your return to that location?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now with the assistance of the usher, I'd like you to mark the location of your command post on this map. Do you see the location of your command post on the map? And I'd ask you not to make any markings yet.

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Could it be lowered a bit southward, the map? Just a bit down, south. [In English] No, no, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. I'd suggest in order to have a better view on how far this is from Sanski Most town, that we slightly zoom in, not too much, slightly, so that we have the outskirts of the town still there and at the same time also -- yes, I think when I said "zoom in" I meant "zoom out," but ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. [Interpretation] May I do it now?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yes. Do you see the location of your command post? If you could indicate that with a number 1.

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Close to this intersection here, I don't know if I'll get the right house but here near Svajba. That's the location. The command post of the company was about ten metres away from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And could you put a number 1 next to that.

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, with the Sana River as your -- or was the Sana River the easterly border of the area of responsibility of your company in this reserve position?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: I've already said that we were at the reserve position in the area of deployment waiting for our next assignment. Quite simply we were resting, the unit was, and we were there. We did not have specific areas of responsibility therefore.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, you say in your statement that the Dabar area was the area of responsibility of the 1st Battalion. I'm just going to get your statement so I'm not misquoting. You say the 1st Infantry Battalion was in the area of -- of Dabar. That's the area that we are all looking at or we're looking at a portion of the Dabar area; correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: We are not looking at the Dabar area now. That's a separate village that cannot be seen from here. From Krkojevci it is to the north-west, a few kilometres, 4 or 5 kilometres north-west. The 1st Battalion in the month of April was indeed in the area of Dabar. Then the companies were deployed, and as I've already said, until mid-May roughly, until I went home to Prijedor somewhere around the 20th or 22nd of May, from there we were withdrawn again to the area of Dabar. Until then we were providing security to the -- at the main bridge in town, Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, in your statement you say that after the June disarmament operations that you were involved in, you again returned to this Krkojevci area, village; correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: We are now saying that on the 30th of May I found the unit in the area of the village of Krkojevci --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: -- after --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: -- that's in your statement. You say you first went to Krkojevci after you returned from Prijedor. You were then involved in disarmament operations in early June. Then you say after this period, your unit returned to the village of Krkojevci. Can you -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Yes. After Hrustovo and that operation, the unit returned to the village of Krkojevci. I'm talking about the beginning of June up until the 13th when we went towards Bihac, the 13th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So you were based in this village of Krkojevci from early June. You left on the 13th and 14th of June when you were in Bihac. Then you returned. And then again you left on the 10th and 11th of July, again to go to Grabez, and then you returned. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender this map as marked by the witness as the next Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31557 as marked by the witness receives number P6892, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, I'd now like to discuss your role in disarmament operations in Hrustovo, which you mentioned today and you mentioned in your statement. Now, what was the date that your unit first entered Hrustovo?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: We did not directly enter Hrustovo. As I said in my statement, we were given the following task: The roads from Begejci, Kenjari should be taken, and we should reach our forces in the village of Korjenovo in the municipality of Kljuc. On that road, on the 2nd of June, we were met by the Muslim units there and there was an armed conflict. So on the 2nd of June, we first set out on that mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So on the 2nd of June you were not in Hrustovo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: On the 2nd of June we were facing the village of Hrustovo, somewhere on the border between the village of Kljevci and Hrustovo. Perhaps part of the unit was in Hrustovo and another part was in the village of Kljevci because we were moving in combat disposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now in your statement you state that three members of the 2nd Infantry Company of your battalion were killed in the village of Hrustovo and that's on the 1st of June, 1992. So I understand from your evidence today that you were not present at that time; correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: No, it was members of the 2nd Infantry Company and I was commander of the 1st Infantry Company, and we are talking about the 1st Infantry Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Okay. Now this Trial Chamber has received evidence that on the 31st of May, 1992, so the day before these events, Serb soldiers killed 27 unarmed non-Serb civilians including children and a pregnant woman who were sheltering in a garage in Hrustovo. Are you aware of these deaths of these non-Serb civilians?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So you've never heard about this incident in this garage in Hrustovo on the 31st of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Later on from the media and in the Vrhpoljski Most case, I heard about some details. But during the war I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So you were facing this village on the 3rd of June, 1992, you were commanding a company of men in that area, yet you have no knowledge about the massacre of these people in that garage a few days earlier to your arrival in the same area; correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: No. Because I was in the area of the village of Krkojevci and I really don't know what was happening during those days. I've already told that you the first time we went towards that village with my unit was on the 2nd of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now in paragraph 13, you discuss your role in the disarming operations in Sanski Most in June 1992. Now, you are aware, are you not, that some of the Muslims disarmed during these mop-up operations were taken to various locations in Sanski Most, yes?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: I came to Sanski Most on the 30th of May and I just heard that the unit took part in disarming the armed formations that were not within the Army of Republika Srpska or Bosnia-Herzegovina. I did not hear about anyone being taken away and my deputy did not tell me about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And after you came to Sanski Most on the 30th of May, after you yourself were involved in these disarming operations, did you hear that members of the 6th Brigade took persons disarmed to a number of different locations in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: First of all, let us be clear on this. On the 31st of May, the unit did not take part in any combats operations or disarming. I'm talking about the 1st Infantry Company. Nothing until the 2nd of June. And now you're asking about the members of the 6th Sana Brigade, whether they took part in such activities. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: In connection with that answer, I'd like to show you a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please could P2900. And I'd like to go to page 14 in the English and 18 in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, we see -- we see that this is a report of the Sanski Most SJB, and it's dated the 18th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please go to page 16 in the English and 21 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And, sir, at the bottom of the page we see that this document is signed by the chief of the SJB, Mirko Vrucinic. You knew this man, yes?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Yes. At the time he was chief of the public security station of Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now could we go back to page 14 in the English, please, and 18 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, in the first paragraph we read that: "During the time of armed combat, two collection and investigation centres were set up in Sanski Most. One, the sports hall, was a collection centre, and one (facilities of the Betonirka enterprise) was a collection and investigation centre. Since 1 August 1992, the sports hall has been empty, and a collection and investigation centre was set up in the Krings factory hall." Sir, are you familiar with the locations referred to in this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: I heard about that but I did not have any common points with them, these locations you mentioned, Betonirka, what was meant specifically. And this factory, Krings, I know where that is but I wasn't present there at the time because that wasn't really my line of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And, sir, I hear that you are saying that you were not present at the time but do I understand your answer to be that you were aware that these were locations that captured Muslims were taken to?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Well, I heard about these places where the soldiers were practically disarmed. I did not hear of all inhabitants of the Muslim faith were being taken away. Just the disarmed members of the Muslim Croat forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Okay. So I understand from your answer that you heard that disarmed members of the Muslim forces were taken to the three locations referred to in this paragraph; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please go to page 16 in the English and 20 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now towards the top of the page in the English and towards the bottom of the page in the B/C/S, we see the heading number III: "The role of the SJB in connection with bringing in, securing, and guarding prisoners in the assembly centres."

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And could we please go to the next page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now in the second paragraph of this section, we read: "Members of the SJB carried operative processing of and provided security for captives both in their collection centres and when they were transferred to Manjaca Army Camp."

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to go --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Or, sir, are you aware that persons were transferred to Manjaca army camp? You've heard about that, yes?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, on this page we see a list and shortly before this list we read the following: "Speaking of records and processing of persons, we inform you that all persons who were operatively processed were simultaneously recorded and we accordingly provide the following details." Now halfway down this list we see: "Escaped during transportation to Manjaca, 20 persons." In the paragraph below this list, we read: "There is official forensic documentation on persons who died, and an official report by the persons responsible for transport concerning the people who escaped (disappeared) while they were being transported to the army camp." Mr. Kolar, do you have any knowledge about these 20 persons who escaped or disappeared while being transported to the Manjaca army camp?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy, one of the lines read "escaped during transportation to the army camp," the other one -- line reads "escaped during transportation to Manjaca." Now, you combined the two and are still talking about 20, you are talking about Manjaca army camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see the ditto marks after 20 which I understood to be replicating the previous part. I'm happy to instead refer to the part saying "escaped during transportation to the army camp, 20 persons."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I'll have a look at the original to see whether that sheds any light on the issue I raised. But the witness doesn't know anything about 20 people escaped, so therefore -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, there is evidence in this case that on or about the 7th of July, 1992, Muslim detainees died of suffocation while being transferred from Betonirka to the Manjaca camp. Do you have any knowledge about this incident?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: No, because my unit did not do that work. It didn't provide security in the camp and it did not escort the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, on the 3rd of November, 2006, the court of Bosnia and Herzegovina convicted Nikola Kovacevic, previously known as Danilusko Kajtez, for among other things, the suffocation of at least 19 detainees, detained civilians who were being transported from Betonirka to Manjaca on the 7th of July, 1992. Now, you are aware of Danilusko Kajtez's conviction in the state court; correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: I have heard of Danilusko Kajtez. I don't know what he was convicted for. I did hear that he was convicted for war crimes, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, you were in the 6th Brigade for over four years and you rose to chief of staff. Danilusko Kajtez was a member of your brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: I did not have the opportunity to see that man or to get to know him. To tell you the truth, 4.000 men passed through the brigade. So I didn't know him personally and I wasn't aware that he was a member of the unit. The first time I heard of him was from the media where I read that he was convicted for war crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think we're at the time for a break or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're close to a time for a break. Witness, we would like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy, we listened for quite a while to the evidence of this witness, mainly consisting in that he doesn't know anything about matters which are covered by some of the evidence the Chamber has received until now. Will this result in any -- or do we just continue for another half-hour hearing that the witness doesn't know anything about what happened because he was just a little bit further away?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I hope that it will become clear to you. I can -- I can certainly explain that to you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: -- now or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there was a -- if you -- if it comes to a point where your next questions will shed more light on the previous answers, then of course we'll wait for that as long as you stay within your time. But how much time would you need for that, to seek that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd hoped to conclude within the next 15 minutes of court time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then you'll stay just within your own time estimate. We'll take a break. We'll resume at 20 minutes to 2.00. We expect you to finish then within 15 -- certainly not more than 20 minutes. Mr. Stojanovic -- or, Mr. Ivetic, how much time would you, as matters stand now, need for --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As matters stand now, no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which means that we try to do our utmost best to have this witness excused today so that they can return home. Mr. Stojanovic, you are concerned about your next witness? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honours. I just need your guidance on that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it may be that there could be 15 minutes left, which we should still use. If it's only three, four, or five minutes, we might decide otherwise. But I'm also relying on the estimates given by the parties that we'll -- that we'll finish to hear the evidence of this witness at approximately 2.00. We resume at 20 minutes to 2.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Just in respect to Exhibit P2900. That was the document the translation of which you queried. We will submit this for retranslation. We understand that where we have these two references to 20 persons, the first reference in B/C/S actually means "succumbed" [Realtime transcript read in error "is commed"] rather than "escaped." I don't think it affects the question that I asked the witness, but I think it is worth submitting for a revised translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And also we see that the translation does not follow exactly the interpunction as we see it on the original, that is persons or --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Ditto marks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yes. We'll ask that to be carefully looked at as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ditto marks you call them. Yes, I understood what you meant but I have to -- it's not my native language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy, if you could just looked at whether you -- the transcript says exactly what you said, "succumbed" or "is commed"? Line 9 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Succumbed. I understood you to say s-u-c-c-u-m-b-e-d. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I'm glad you did the spelling, Your Honour. But yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Were you not able to do it?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Of course, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kolar, I'd like to finish today by discussing the mass grave in which the bodies that I've been referring to was found. Now, the 3rd of November, 2006, state court judgement that I referred to in represent to Danilusko Kajtez noted that the 19 bodies were identified and exhumed at the mass grave site Usce Dabar in Sanski Most. Now, that is a location that is known to you; correct?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Yes, it's where the Dabar River flows into the Sana River.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we call up 65 ter 12331, please. And this is the court record of exhumation Usce Dabar dated the 24th of November, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is an exhumation report from the cantonal court in Bihac dated the 24th of September, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And if we go to the last page, please, in each document, we see that it is signed by the investigating judge. Thank you. And if we could go back to page 1, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, in the first paragraph of this document, we read that the record of exhumation relates to two mass graves: One found in the location of Usce Dabar and another in the Tomina Markovici area, both in Sanski Most. I want to focus on the mass grave found in Usce Dabar.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please go to page 2 in each language.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, halfway down the page we see description of scene. We read: "On the 17th of July, 2001, at the locality of Usce Dabar," co-ordinates are given, "exhumation commenced of a mass grave with 19 bodies, most of which were skeletonised and some saponified." Now, in the next paragraph we read: "The location in question is in the area of Sanski Most municipality, near the centre of town, at a distance of around 3 kilometres at the section of the road running upstream along with the Sana River to the SG of the Dabar River on the left bank of the Sana River at a distance of around 100 metres from the Dabar river, in a narrowed part of the property (meadow) in the village of Krkojevci." And we read: "The owner of the property is not known." Sir, are you familiar with the location of the mass grave as described in this document? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now to finish I'd like to show you a final map, and it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I've read the relevant portion of this document that I'm relying on. I won't tender it. Could we please go to 65 ter 31558.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is the same map of Sanski Most that we saw earlier with one exception, that exception is that the OTP has marked -- that the Office of the Prosecutor has marked on this map with a red dot the location of the mass grave according to the co-ordinates described in the exhumation report. Now, you've told us earlier today that you and your unit were in the village of Krkojevci in July 1992, other than for two days on the 10th and the 11th of July. Now, a mass grave of 19 people requires a great deal of activity, sir, and as the commander of the company in this village, I put it to you that you must have known about the creation of this mass grave at the time it was created in July 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I object to the foundation of the question. Where do we have evidence that the grave was from July of 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, the evidence that I've referred to indicates that the persons, the 19 persons who were killed on the 7th of July, I would submit that it is a reasonable inference to suggest to the witness that the grave itself was dated around a similar time -- was created at a similar time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Unless we have evidence that it's a primary grave. I mean, we don't have any of that, do we? There is many graves --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- that could be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would rephrase the question in such a way that the witness understands that this is an inference from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, there is evidence in this case that 19 persons, 19 Muslim civilians died while being transported from Betonirka to Manjaca camp on the 7th of July, 1992. It is the position of the Prosecution that this mass grave in which these 19 persons were found was created on or shortly after the 7th of July, 1992. We see here that this grave was created in the village or near the village of Krkojevci where you yourself was located in July, and I put it to you that you must have been aware of the creation of this mass grave at that time.

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: I don't know. You don't sound convincing. But I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So you have no knowledge whatsoever about this mass grave or the creation of it in your area, in your village?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: No. This is the first time that I hear of this. Let me clarify once again: The unit was in the upper part of Krkojevci. I've already showed that to you. 200 metres. That's where my entire unit was. As far as I can see, this location is at least 2 kilometres away, perhaps even more than that, from the location where my unit was.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And do I understand, then, that you'd never heard at all about the creation of this mass grave in the village where you were located at time-periods during the war?

utterances.speaker: RANKO KOLAR
utterances.text: Yes. This is the first time that I hear of this grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I would tender this exhibit as created by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Defence would object. Based upon the evidence and the representations that have been made of date, we would not object to it being MFI'd. And if the Prosecution wishes to present evidence of how the map was marked, based upon what investigator did it, based upon what technique, as they have with other such exhibits, either by way of declaration or by testimony, then we would not have an objection. But based upon just the representation that the OTP put a point on a map doesn't, I think, suffice for -- for our purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, wouldn't it be reasonable that if you have the grid details, that you just check whether it's accurately done or not; if so, to not further make any fuss about it, and if not, to make a lot of fuss about it? I mean, we have the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you show me where the grid details are on this particular map, Your Honour? It does not have the longitude and latitude lines identified as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd -- I mean, I would suggest that we MFI this document to give Mr. Ivetic an opportunity to verify the -- the co-ordinates within a time-period after which I'd stand by my request for it to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How can I verify if I don't have the base map that is in the Prosecution's possession? That is my point, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would like to have a look at the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. Because I have -- I have this. I can't do anything with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The objection is denied. The witness testified about what he saw on this map. It was -- he explained that this was at a distance from where he was located with his unit at that point in time. Now whether or not the picture -- whether the red marking corresponds with what is found in that other report, which is not in evidence, Mr. Jeremy, you did not --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: It's not in evidence, but I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but of course that document gives the details of where that locality was. I mean, that's -- on the second page you have read that out but you have said co-ordinates --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- are there without reading them out so to see whether they correspond with what we find on the map. Because the document read that it's at 32.243-53.124, and that's exactly what appears on the map. Now, of course, another matter is whether it's plotted well on the map, yes or no, which of course may shed some light as to how to understand the testimony of this witness. Mr. Ivetic may finally come to the conclusion that it was even closer to where the witness's units was or further away or at exactly the location. It is a matter I would suggest the parties could try to agree upon. But since the witness has testified about the matter and what he said, to understand that testimony we need this map. And it does not automatically mean that the location is marked accurately and corresponding with what we find in the report in which I just read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And after the witness has been discharged, I'll invite Mr. Ivetic to see if we can reach agreement about the -- this particular location on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would be appreciated. I take it that Mr. Ivetic would make himself available for such a consultation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, the objection being denied, what would be the number of the map as marked -- not as marked by the witness but as marked by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31558 receives number P6893, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Any further questions, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We have no questions. We would just thank Mr. Kolar again for his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There may be a small mistake in the transcript. Page 83, line 12. Madam Registrar -- Madam Registrar's recollection is that she mentioned P6893. This concludes your evidence in this court, Mr. Kolar. I would like to thank you very much for having coming to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again and we are happy that we can release you still today.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if the next witness would be ready, then we would like him to be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Bojanovic is your next witness. Mr. Stojanovic, you'll examine him?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just say that I have also reduced the list of exhibits in accordance with the guidance you gave us, so I will have eight along with the statement of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's appreciated. Still slightly above the guidance of five, but I take it that the Prosecution doesn't take any issue with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi will be handling this witness, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we know that for sure -- no, Mr. Traldi, do you take any issue with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The number?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We had no issue with the number. Depending on -- obviously a number of these relate to particular cases, it may be that we would request that one or two more come in depending on the selections the Defence has made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Bojanovic. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. The text is handed out to you. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Stojanovic. You'll find Mr. Stojanovic to your left. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Bojanovic.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: For the record, could you please speak slowly and state your exact name and surname.

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I am Savo Bojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, at one point in time did you give a statement in writing to General Mladic's Defence?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please have 65 ter 1D01732 in e-court, please. And could we take a look at the first page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, you have the document in front of you and this is what I'm asking you. Is this your signature on this page and are your details correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's my signature and the details are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now take a look at the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, on this page of the document do we also see your signature and is the date that is handwritten on this page written in your own hand?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is on the 28th of July this year that I signed this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In preparation for your testimony in court, did you indicate two typographical errors to me that need to be corrected?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Three, not two.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for the correction. We'll see whether it's an error or an addition.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could we please take a look at paragraph 11 in this document; that is, the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bojanovic, in the second subparagraph, did you tell me that this date that is stated here; namely, this is how it reads: "To the best of my recollection, on the 30th of December, 1992," et cetera. Should it say the 30th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That would be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have paragraph 16 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 16 of your statement. Mr. Bojanovic, did you indicate to me that here in this sentence which starts with the following words, "In the second half of 1992, it was held," et cetera, did you say that it should read "1993"?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that would be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And did you also indicate to me that in that sentence, by way of clarification, after the words "perpetrators of crimes committed in the course of military duty," should the word "military" be added?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So would we agree then that this sentence would correctly read, I'm reading this out for the transcript now: "In the second half of 1992 [as interpreted], it was held that the military courts should try perpetrators of crimes committed in the course of military duty and that all other crimes were to be under the jurisdiction of regular courts." Would that be the correct text in this sentence?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, may I just correct. What you are recorded now, instead of "1992" it's going to read "1993," I think? "1993." In line with your previous correction. It should read "in the second of half of 1993 ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour. Line 87 -- no, page 87, line 13 of the transcript, it should read "1993." That would be correct. Thank you, Your Honour. And now I would like to ask that we look at paragraph 19. I'm sorry, paragraph 25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt. I hadn't caught where the additional word "military" was appearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before the word "duty" in --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It -- so it was because it already appeared in the English that I -- I didn't realise. That's my mistake. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No problem. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And now paragraph 25, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: While preparing for your testimony in court, did we establish that there is something missing in the last sentence? It says here: "By in the judgement in this case, the accused was sentenced to a suspended term of imprisonment of four months with a probation period of one year." And the words "and six months" should be added?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now that we've made these corrections, Mr. Bojanovic, and now that you took the oath in this courtroom, this statement that was provided, is it truthful, complete, and based on your best recollection?

utterances.speaker: SAVO BOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender the statement of Witness Savo Bojanovic, 1D01732 being its 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Have you asked the witness already whether he would give the same answers if being asked the same questions? Would you give the same answers, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. Traldi? Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1732 receives number D747, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D747 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honours, I would like to read a brief summary of Witness Savo Bojanovic's statement. When the war broke out, Witness Savo Bojanovic was in Bijeljina where he had a law office of his own. When the military court in Bijeljina was established, since it was necessary and since he held the appropriate professional qualifications, he was appointed judge in this court. He remained in that position until the end of 1993 when he transferred to a different duty. In his statement he speaks about internal organisation and personnel, subject matter jurisdiction, and the tasks that the military judiciary had during the war. He points out that the work of the court was based only on respect for and implementation of the law. All perpetrators of crimes were treated equally by the court, regardless of their religious or ethnic affiliation. He personally as a judge tried Serbs, inter alia, for crimes committed against non-Serbs. In his statement he analysed some cases like that and he says that he personally never received any orders as to how he should try cases, and he never heard that any of his colleagues had received suggestions as to how they should work and how they should try cases. The court also carried out no discrimination whatsoever on the basis of religious or ethnic affiliation of the accused persons or injured parties. The witness says that when the military judiciary started operating, there was a dispute in terms of jurisdiction between regular courts and military courts. So there was a question raised: Namely, who would try the perpetrators of individual crimes. Then in the second half of 1993, finally the position was taken that military courts should try perpetrators of crimes if the crimes were committed in the course of military duty. Their relationship with regular courts was proper and based on the law. Finally, the witness says that any claim that he personally knew of the alleged killings of 40 to 80 civilians perpetrated by members of MUP of Republika Srpska would constitute a fabrication and lie because he has no information about that. Your Honours, that would be a brief summary of this witness's statement. Perhaps I could end within the next five minutes. I see the time, so it is for you to say whether I should finish the direct today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, unfortunately we are not able to continue at this moment. But we took note of the fact that you need only five minutes for examination-in-chief. So therefore, those five minutes are available for you tomorrow. Witness, Mr. Bojanovic, I would like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, whether already given, not much today but already given today or still to be given tomorrow, not to speak with anyone or to communicate in any other way. And we would like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 in this same courtroom. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day and will resume tomorrow, Wednesday -- Thursday, the 6th of November, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 6th day of November, 2014, at 9.30 a.m.
